description: Add a prospecting guide to the Info / Cargo overlay so players can understand ore values, unlock depths, and early mining goals without leaving the game.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh and inspect the current Info / Cargo overlay and early-game HUD before editing.

Inspect src/ui.tsx, src/dom.ts, src/game.ts, src/constants.ts, src/styles.css, and existing UI/economy tests for the current info dialog, ore constants, cargo detail rendering, and mobile layout constraints.

Add a DOM-free helper that formats the ORES table into concise prospecting-guide rows, converting ore minimum rows into player-facing depth labels using START_Y and preserving ore value/color data for UI rendering.

Extend the Info / Cargo overlay with a compact Prospecting Guide section that lists each ore's name, value, approximate starting depth, and color marker, plus one short tip that the first Coal/Copper seam appears near the starting shaft.

Keep existing DOM IDs/classes consumed by the runtime intact; add any new stable DOM hooks to src/dom.ts only if the runtime needs them, and ensure the overlay stays readable on narrow/mobile layouts without covering critical HUD controls when closed.
Add or update tests for the prospecting-guide helper and React shell markup so future changes catch stale ore values/depth labels and preserve the new in-game guidance.
Run ./init.sh and perform a live browser/CDP smoke that opens Info / Cargo after starting the game, confirms the guide is visible, mines or moves briefly, and reports no runtime exceptions.
acceptance: From live gameplay, opening Info / Cargo shows a readable Prospecting Guide with ore names, cash values, approximate depth thresholds, and color markers derived from the current ORES constants.

The guide gives early players a clear next goal after the current observed state of $60 cash, 20 m depth, empty cargo, and next Cargo +10 needing $60 more, without requiring external README knowledge.
Existing cargo list, controls help, Sound affordance, intro flow, keyboard/touch movement, and HUD feedback remain intact with no runtime exceptions.
Before marking complete, run ./test.sh plus canonical verification npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build.
